rationale.conceptual: The method involves first-principles DFT for harmonic and anharmonic force constants and the relaxation-time approximation BTE with non-standard extrinsic scattering models (grain-boundary, point-defect). It is a well-documented, published technique but requires understanding of phonon physics, scattering mechanisms, and correct integration of several components. Not entirely textbook but not novel research-grade (3).
rationale.execution: The pipeline includes DFT supercell calculations for anharmonic force constants, post-processing with a BTE solver, and applying multiple scattering models. This involves at least two major tool stages (DFT code + ShengBTE) with careful convergence and coupling. No complex data acquisition or massive orchestration, but the multi-step, dependency-laden workflow with non-trivial parameterization places it at 3.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires a full first-principles + phonon BTE pipeline: DFT harmonic/anharmonic force constants, then solving the Boltzmann equation with extrinsic scattering models. This is a multi-step, well-established but non-trivial computational method in condensed matter physics. No novel algorithms are needed, but careful implementation of the BTE with grain-boundary and point-defect scattering adds moderate conceptual complexity. The pipeline involves DFT (e.g., Quantum ESPRESSO) and a BTE solver (ShengBTE), which are standard but require proper concatenation and parameterization. Overall, conceptual complexity is moderate (3), and execution is a multi-stage pipeline with non-trivial tooling (3). Resource needs: the reference estimate assumes ~7 hours on a GPU for the DFT anharmonic force constants, so a GPU (likely A100-class) and substantial memory are needed; input data is tiny.
